rationale: Matthew's "Do not judge, or you will be judged" (7:1, BSB) and Luke's Sermon on the Plain both open on judgment, but Luke's wording is fuller at this specific point: "Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven" (6:37, BSB) -- a three-part set Matthew's own text does not carry at 7:1. The measure clause is close but not identical: Matthew has "with the measure you use, it will be measured to you" (7:2, BSB); Luke has "with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you" (6:38, BSB), adding "back" where Matthew's own wording does not. The speck-and-beam saying that follows is the most tightly matched material in this pair: "Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?" (7:3, BSB) is close to word for word identical to Luke's "Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?" (6:41, BSB), and the hypocrite-rebuke sentence that closes each version (7:5; 6:42, both BSB) matches as well. The type is parallel (two Gospel records of the same teaching material, neither quoting the other by formula); the label is strong because both the close verbal overlap and the specific points where the two versions diverge (Luke's three-part judge/condemn/forgive set; the "back" in Luke's measure clause) are both directly checkable against each Gospel's own shipped BSB text.
